CausalChain: NAFLD-induced metabolic stress -> Upregulation of FTO demethylase in hepatocytes -> FTO-mediated removal of m6A marks on lipid metabolism regulatory mRNAs -> Increased stability and translation of lipogenic and metabolic reprogramming transcripts -> Enhanced lipogenesis and altered energy homeostasis -> Predisposition of hepatocytes to malignant transformation -> Development of HCC
Hypothesis: In NAFLD-driven liver disease, upregulation of the m6A demethylase FTO leads to site-specific removal of m6A modifications on mRNAs that encode key lipid metabolism regulators. This demethylation stabilizes these transcripts, promoting metabolic reprogramming in hepatocytes that facilitates the transition from NAFLD to hepatocellular carcinoma.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has been closely linked to dysregulated m6A RNA modification, with emerging evidence implicating m6A regulators in controlling key oncogenic processes. Here, we propose a novel hypothesis that aberrant m6A demethylation, particularly mediated by the FTO enzyme in the context of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), selectively stabilizes mRNAs encoding critical lipid metabolism regulators. This enhanced stability leads to metabolic reprogramming in hepatocytes, thereby promoting the progression from NAFLD to HCC. Our model integrates metabolic stress with epitranscriptomic dysregulation and suggests that m6A-modified mRNAs, when demethylated by FTO, drive changes in lipid biosynthesis and energy homeostasis that set the stage for malignant transformation. Testing this hypothesis may uncover new diagnostic biomarkers and targeted therapeutic strategies in liver cancer.
